terra.problem: The passage tells more about the two men, including Pelatiah's death, so saying that is all it tells us about them is inaccurate.
“I won't add more” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The oven joke doesn't match the comparison: a gatekeeper is a person associated with a gate, not the gate itself.
The text doesn't say the gate is quiet.
The text says the men plot evil and give wicked counsel in the city, not necessarily at the gate.
“So people listen” adds a response to their counsel that the text doesn't give.
The claim that there would be no trouble at the gate if the men hated evil goes beyond the text.
“So Ezekiel can't miss it” supplies a reason for the repeated command that the text doesn't give.
The verse doesn't say the thoughts God knows are underneath the words spoken at the gate.
The text doesn't say the men used the pot picture to say they were safe.
The passage doesn't say the men meant the city was a safe pot.
The hiding-in-a-pot joke makes light of the threatened violence.
The quote uses “I” without first identifying Ezekiel as the speaker. “I won't either” also comments on how Papa tells the passage.
“I'll leave it as the text has it” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The text says Pelatiah died while Ezekiel was prophesying, but doesn't say Ezekiel watched it happen right in front of him.
The text doesn't establish that nobody in Jerusalem was giving titles to the exiles. “That's the whole opinion” also omits what the people said about possessing the land.
The explanation is generic and repeats the answer without adding much of Papa's voice.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer with little of Papa's voice.
The claim that the glory had been at the east gate earlier in the vision needs a reference to the other passage, such as Ezekiel 10:19.
The quote uses “I” without first identifying Ezekiel as the speaker.
